title: TESS CPV flags permit month-long dip episodes in a persistent low-rate stellar state
abstract: We test whether long memory of complex periodic variable (CPV) flags requires long material supply episodes or a state with no capacity to make dips. We extend a published three-state model to four states with positive high and low dip rates. We reuse 245 flags from 8,772 TESS sectors of 1,746 stars. The source model is recovered at zero low-state duty, with log likelihood -632.042. At low-state duty 0.001 the log likelihood is -630.815. The example has mean low-state on episodes of 29.4 days and off intervals of 80.5 years, conditional on a fixed rate state. It retains a 70.8-year rate-state correlation time. This is an allowed alternative, not a detection of rare material. A coupling bound shows that duty 10^-6 changes the probability distribution of the full experiment by at most 0.008772 in total variation distance. Thus finite flags cannot distinguish zero capacity from a sufficiently rare positive rate without a minimum-rate assumption. A two-window moment example gives the same result. The evidence for persistent stellar differences and fewer high-rate stars with age remains. The host correlation limit does not by itself bound a general material lifetime. The result depends on the inherited flag and efficiency model and adds no physical mass or supply constraint. Code, input hashes, aggregate fits and independent forward-algorithm checks are supplied.

display.caption: Positive low-state dip rates fit the released flags. Long stellar rate-state memory permits on episodes of about one month in the model.
Under an idealized two-window model, rate distributions with different fractions of positive-rate stars have identical first and second moments.
